blurb_title: The CA's key sits as a Kubernetes Secret in etcd. Anyone with get secrets can issue certificates. Nobody finds out.
blurb_1: This guide moves the CA into OpenBao: root and intermediate as separate mounts, a role that dictates domains, key type and lifetime, and cert-manager that only sends CSRs. Ingress by annotation, service-to-service by Certificate, chain verified against Traefik.
blurb_2: With two rejections, the first of which was not the expected one: role requires keys of type ec came before not allowed by this role. Plus renewal with a new key, revocation on the CRL, and why set-signed creates two issuers.
code: -- The only thing that ever leaves OpenBao: a CSR bao write -field=csr pki_int/intermediate/generate/internal … bao write pki/root/sign-intermediate csr=@pki_int.csr … bao write pki_int/intermediate/set-signed certificate=@pki_int.pem
